_what: Per-platform strategy, learned from our own numbers. The Analyst updates it every night (Justin 11-19: learn after every post, keep adjusting each platform until it's mastered). The Scheduler uses 'route' to decide which clip goes to which platform; the Clip Finder uses 'want' to decide what to look for. Evidence lines are dated; small samples are marked as such.
_updated: 2026-11-19 17:30 ET, main chat (first review: 16 TikTok, 13 Instagram, 4 Facebook, 18 YouTube, 1 X post)
cross_platform: The same clip lands very differently per platform, so routing matters more than volume: BP traffic = IG 1,385 / TT 227 / YT 1; LACY Part 2 (dying costs ALL your money) = IG 1,534 / FB 475 / YT 28 / TT 16; Speed download countdown = YT 1,366 / IG 153 / TT 0.
A slot may carry two different clips split by platform (e.g. 18:10: story clip to IG+FB, mechanic clip to TT+YT) when that fits better. Daily caps per platform still hold.

tiktok.health_metric: For You share per post (Metricool TKPO16). Healthy >= 0.7. Under 0.3 on most posts = account throttled.
tiktok.status: throttled: after ~13 posts on day one, 12 of the next 14 posts got 0-49 views with For You 0-20%.
what_works: 15-20 s clips with a GTA 6 mechanic/frustration stated plainly and a reaction in second 1: 'LACY can't steal cars the old way' (15 s, 250 views, 9 s avg watch, 93% For You); 'Burnt Peanut vs GTA 6 traffic' (30 s, 227 views, 10 s avg).
avoid: reposting a moment (BP traffic repost: 8 views)
Speed clips (0 views on TikTok, heavily clipped by others)

experiment.name: recover reach
experiment.plan: While For You stays under 0.3: post only the single best mechanic clip a day (15-22 s) at 11:10 or 18:10. Back to 3 a day after 2 posts in a row with For You >= 0.6.

instagram.health_metric: Reel skip rate (IGRE30, swiped in first 3 s): target under 30%. Views + shares.
what_works: Relatable GTA 6 'pain' mechanics told as a plain fact: LACY Part 2 'dying in GTA 6 takes ALL your money' 1,534 views (25% skip, 12.9 s avg watch); BP 'zero patience for GTA 6 traffic' 1,385 (25% skip, 10 shares).
Shares drive it: the two clips with 10 shares are both top-3.
A Part 2 that works as a standalone beats its Part 1 (1,534 vs 152).
avoid: openers that need context: 'LACY's first bank job' had 60% skip and 7 views

experiment.name: captions A/B
experiment.plan: Word-by-word vs phrase captions (split test running since 11-19, build.json). Compare skip rate and avg watch after ~20 Reels.

facebook.health_metric: Views per Reel and avg watch time (FBRE10, FBRE13).
facebook.status: steady: every Reel with data got 344-589 views (4 Reels, small sample)
what_works: Story and relationship moments: 'LACY forgot to meet Lucia at the bank' 589 views ("I'm a terrible boyfriend").
Part series carry on Facebook: Part 1 344, Part 2 475.

experiment.name: series vs standalone
experiment.plan: Alternate Part series and standalone story clips; compare views per Reel after 6 Reels.

youtube.health_metric: Views after 48 h per Short and any 'Potential limitation' label in YouTube Studio.
youtube.status: one hit, most Shorts stuck at 0-28 views; 'Potential limitation' on BP driving
what_works: Big name + big moment people search for: Speed counting down the GTA 6 download, 1,366 views (native upload by the Speed chat).
LACY's first Lucia reaction, 205 views (first upload).
avoid: uploading the same moment twice (BP traffic went up twice)
generic reactions without a searchable topic

route.title_style: searchable: '<Streamer> <does/finds> <GTA 6 thing>' with the GTA 6 topic words people search

experiment.name: search titles
experiment.plan: Titles that lead with the GTA 6 topic ('GTA 6 cars run out of gas? LACY found out') vs name-first. Compare 48 h views after 8 Shorts.

x.health_metric: Views per post in the first 2 h (X weighs early engagement).
x.status: just started (1 post: Clix plane, 38 views in 5 h)

experiment.plan: Alternate an IG winner and a fresh clip; compare 24 h views after 8 posts.
